title: Theseus and Athens
subtitle: Founders, civic myth, and contested versions

assessment.title: Theseus and Athens assessment
assessment.prompt: Five new questions revisit the week’s events, interpretations, and source distinctions. Taking the assessment completes the week; missed answers remain practice priorities.

question.prompt: Which source supplies this biographical framing?
question.explanation: Plutarch’s Life of Theseus. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

question.prompt: What does the thread qualify about the heroic victory?

choices.text: Theseus needs no knowledge of the maze.
Theseus’ success depends on another person’s practical aid.
The Minotaur has already left Crete.

question.explanation: Theseus’ success depends on another person’s practical aid.. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

question.prompt: What changes when the hero becomes a civic founder?

choices.text: His story ceases to have political meaning.
The source becomes an eyewitness record of prehistoric Athens.
His deeds explain the community’s institutions and belonging.

question.explanation: His deeds explain the community’s institutions and belonging.. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

choices.text: Plutarch reports alternatives; his report does not establish one eyewitness history.
All variants must have happened consecutively.
A later biography cannot preserve any earlier traditions.

question.explanation: Plutarch reports alternatives; his report does not establish one eyewitness history.. Revisit the named passage and distinguish its narrative from the lesson’s interpretation.

question.prompt: What evidence is needed for the comparison?
